title: Gemini desktop to get broader Computer Use permissions
key_facts: TestingCatalog spotted a new 'Additional sandbox options' setting under the computer use section of the Gemini desktop app.
Its description suggests Gemini could operate outside selected folders, access the internet and work across other apps without asking approval for every step.
High-stakes actions, including purchases or approving legal documents, would still need human confirmation.
The capability is currently associated with trusted testing, and Google has not announced when it will reach regular users.
Other unreleased desktop features in development include Tasks Mode and a revamped Gemini Spark.

Google officially introduced Gemini 4 Argon on 30 Sep 2026, first for selected cybersecurity experts through its Fairwind programme, and is evaluating it for computer use; Google has not confirmed any link to the desktop app capabilities.
TestingCatalog says presence in trusted testing gives no reliable launch date; some Gemini features ship quickly, others stay gated for months.
quote_evidence: TestingCatalog recently spotted a new “Additional sandbox options” setting under the computer use section.
The capability is currently associated with trusted testing, and Google has not announced when it will reach regular users.
However, Google has not confirmed any connection between Argon and the capabilities now appearing in the Gemini desktop app.
why_it_matters_hint: Google may be preparing to let Gemini work across a whole computer with fewer prompts, but nothing is confirmed or dated.
event_date: Not stated ('recently spotted'); TestingCatalog published it on 2 Oct 2026.
notes: One outlet reading an unreleased setting; the story is about a possible feature, not a launch.
